claim_being_audited: That the model should be certified for launch on the current record, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a draft monitoring-and-rollback mitigation, without needing stronger limitation disclosure support or a fully approved mitigation artifact.
decision_criteria: If current admissible evidence showed no material weakness remained for the named launch use case, certification would be supportable.
If there were an approved mitigation or risk acceptance with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, certification with the required policy support could be justified.
If the limitation is material and neither resolved nor covered by approved risk acceptance, it must be disclosed before launch under the policy note.
Public NIST/model-card guidance can support monitoring and documentation rationale, but it does not substitute for the internal policy predicates required for launch certification.

Provide decision evidence on whether the claims subrogation weakness is material for the named launch use case.
Provide the final model-card language showing the limitation is either disclosed or formally determined non-material with supporting rationale.
Provide current evaluation evidence showing the subrogation/liability summarization weakness has been resolved to target, if that is the basis for certification.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows an unresolved weakness in the claims subrogation review slice, concentrated in liability evidence summarization.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure predicate in the policy text.
unsupported_claims: Any implicit claim that certification is compliant without a material caveat is unsupported on the current admissible record.
